messages.text: i'm trying to update harlolabs on my bs2 but it won't let me connect, it doesn't recognize it as a bs 2, i could connect as a bs1 or bs4 but not bs2
I'll check the Harlo OS page for the BS2 device options.
Read harlolabs.com
Searched the web · Harlo OS flasher BS2 not recognized Bitaxe
Let me check the Harlo OS page for the current device list.
Read heliumdeploy.com/blogs/mining-news/harlo-os
Now the flasher's model list.
Read harlolabs.com
Searched the web · Bitfortun BS-2 Harlo OS profile support

Hi, I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Picking this up from Sarah.

That pattern (BS-1 and BS-4 connect, BS-2 does not) usually means the BS-2 profile is checking the controller chip and flash size on your board and not getting the match it expects, rather than a bad cable or port.

One thing first, so I give you the right fix and not a guess:

1. On the flasher page at harlolabs.com, pick BS-2 and try again.
2. Send me a screenshot of the exact message it gives when it refuses (the full line, including anything like ESP32, ESP32-S3, 8MB or 16MB).
3. Also tell me the installer version shown on that page, and which browser (Chrome or Edge).

While you grab that, two quick things worth trying:

- Hold the BOOT button on the board, plug the USB in while holding it, then release and hit connect. That forces download mode.
- Make sure nothing else has the COM port open (serial monitor, another flasher tab).

Send me that error text and I will tell you exactly what it is rejecting.
Downloading and verifying the selected factory image…

Thanks, that is useful. It means the flasher connected fine and is stalling on the BS-2 image itself, not on your board. So this is the image fetch, not your hardware.

Two things:

1. How long does it sit on that line? If it is past a minute or two with no progress bar moving, it is not going to finish.
2. Do a hard refresh of the page (Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R on Mac), pick BS-2 again and watch that same step. If your browser has an ad blocker or a VPN on, turn them off for that tab first, since both can quietly block the image download.

If it stalls at the same line again, tell me and also open the browser console (F12, Console tab) and send me a screenshot of any red error lines. That will show whether the BS-2 image is missing on the server or your network is dropping it.
it doesn't change from this
Handed to the team · Server-side Harlo OS BS-2 factory image appears unavailable; only JD can check o

That confirms it: your board and USB link are fine (BS-1 and BS-4 get past that step), and the BS-2 factory image itself is not coming down. That is on the Harlo side, not something you can fix from your end, so please do not keep retrying or flash a BS-1 or BS-4 image to your BS-2, that would give it the wrong chip count and settings.

I have passed this to JD, who builds Harlo OS. The team has it and will confirm by email, usually within one business day. If you stay in this chat, one of them can jump straight in.

Fastest route if you want it looked at right now: the Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , drop it in the Harlo OS channel and mention @nullhashrate (JD). He is very active there and can push a fixed BS-2 image quickly.

Your unit keeps mining on its current firmware in the meantime, so nothing is lost by waiting.
i tried discord, don't know how to get around, i must of did something wrong yesterday because i was removed,

No problem, you do not need Discord for this. Stay right here in this chat: JD has already been pinged and the team can answer you here, and they will confirm by email too.

I cannot see or change Discord accounts myself, but I have left a note with your case that you were removed from the server yesterday, so the team can look at it when they pick this up.

In the meantime, leave your BS-2 on the firmware it has now and let it keep hashing. Nothing to do on your side until the BS-2 image is fixed.
i was able to get back in today but dont have any message rights

Good, that is often just the server's entry step rather than a restriction.

Two things to check on Discord:

1. Look for a channel like #rules, #welcome or #start at the top of the channel list and accept the rules there (usually a button or a reaction). On most servers posting stays locked until you do that.
2. If Discord asks you to verify your email or phone on your account, do that too. Unverified accounts get read-only in a lot of servers.

That said, you do not need Discord to get this solved. JD has your case from here, and the team can reply in this chat and by email. The Discord was only the faster lane.
is top or bottom boot button or are they the same thing

No, they are not the same. On these boards there are two buttons next to the USB-C port: one is BOOT (sometimes marked IO0) and the other is RST or EN (reset). You want BOOT, and pressing reset instead just restarts the unit.

Which one is in which position varies by board revision, so rather than guess: take a close photo of the board around the USB-C port with the labels visible and send it here, and I will point at the right one.

One thing to keep in mind though: your flasher is stalling at "downloading and verifying the image", which happens before it ever talks to the board. So BOOT mode will not change that stall. It is worth knowing for later, but the BS-2 image fix has to come from JD's side.
is there an easy way to get photos from phone to here

Easiest way: open heliumdeploy.com in your phone's browser, tap the same chat bubble, and use the attach (paperclip) button to pick the photo from your camera roll. No transfer needed.

If you would rather stay on the computer, email the photo to yourself or use Google Photos / iCloud Photos on the desktop, then drag the file into the chat box here.

Either works. Take it with good light, straight down on the board near the USB-C port, close enough that the little white text next to the buttons is readable.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

I opened it. I can see the top edge of the board: the USB-C socket in the middle, with one small white tactile button on each side of it, left and right. The shot is taken from the edge, so the silkscreen text on the board face is not in frame, which is exactly the text I need to tell them apart.

Two options:

1. Send one more photo looking straight down onto the board face (not from the edge), so the little printed labels next to each button are readable. Usually something like BOOT or IO0 on one, RST or EN on the other.
2. Or identify it yourself without labels: with the miner powered up and running normally, press the right-hand button briefly. If the screen blanks and the unit reboots, that one is RESET, so the other one is BOOT. If nothing happens, that one is BOOT.

Option 2 is safe, a short press does nothing harmful either way.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Opened it. That is a LilyGO T-Display-S3 controller module: I can read "T_Display_S3 22-8-2 V1.2" in the silkscreen, the USB-C port on the left edge, and "RST" printed next to the button at the bottom left corner of the board.

So you have your answer:

1. The button with RST printed beside it is reset. Do not use that one for flashing.
2. The other button, on the opposite side of the USB-C port, is BOOT (IO0). That is the one you hold while plugging in.

Also useful: that module is an ESP32-S3. I have added that to the note for JD, since the BS-2 profile mismatch you first hit is a controller and flash size check.

Your flasher is still stalling before it reaches the board though, so BOOT will not clear that stall. Keep the unit mining as is and wait for JD on the BS-2 image.
i had 0.1.49 on it but with that running i checked for updates and it didn't show the new 0.2.101 update

That fits the same picture. Two things are going on, and only one is yours.

Why the update check shows nothing: a jump from 0.1.49 to 0.2.101 is a major version step, and the in-UI OTA check only offers images from the same BS-2 profile on the server, which is the thing that is not serving right now. So the UI honestly has nothing to show you.

There is one route worth trying that skips the flasher entirely:

1. On harlolabs.com, instead of the browser flasher, look for the OTA image download for the BS-2 (a .bin file, not the factory image).
2. In your miner's web UI, go to the firmware or update section and upload that .bin manually.
3. OTA keeps your wifi, your pools and your display theme. The factory image would wipe them.

If the OTA .bin downloads fine, you are updated without touching the BOOT button. If that download also stalls or the page has no BS-2 OTA file, then both BS-2 images are affected, and that is confirmation for JD.

Tell me which of the two you see and I will take it from there. The team can read this whole chat when they jump in.
download factory image and download ota

Perfect, that is exactly what I hoped you would see. Use the OTA one.

1. Click "Download OTA" for the BS-2 and let the .bin file land on your computer.
2. Tell me the file name and size once it is down (it should be a few megabytes, not a few kilobytes). If it arrives as 0 KB or an HTML file, the server side is still broken and we stop there.
3. If it looks right, open your miner's web UI, go to the firmware / update section, choose that .bin and upload it.

Leave the factory image alone. That one erases your wifi and pool settings, and it is also the one that was stalling.

Send me the file name when it finishes.
2.4mb

2.4 MB is a healthy OTA image, so the file is good. Go ahead and flash it from the web UI:

1. Open your miner's web UI in the browser (the miner's IP address).
2. Go to Settings, then the firmware / update section.
3. Choose the OTA .bin you just downloaded and start the upload.
4. Do not unplug the miner and do not close the tab while it writes. It takes a minute or so, then the unit reboots on its own.

Two notes: use Ethernet or a solid wifi signal for this, a drop mid-upload is the one thing that can leave it unhappy. And if the UI also offers a separate "www" or display image, do the main firmware one first.

Tell me what version it shows after the reboot.
i did that but it is just spinning now it won't upload file

Stop and do not unplug it yet. First tell me one thing:

Is the miner's own screen still showing its normal hashing display, and is it still hashing?

- If yes, nothing has been written to flash yet. The upload posts the whole file before it starts writing, so a spinner with no progress means it never got that far. Your unit is safe.
- If the screen has gone blank or shows a progress or update message, leave it completely alone and tell me, because that one is mid-write.

Assuming the screen is normal, do this:

1. Wait two more minutes. If nothing moves, close that tab.
2. Open the miner's IP again in a fresh tab. If it loads and still says 0.1.49, nothing was changed.
3. Retry the upload from Chrome or Edge specifically, on a wired connection if you can, with the miner also on Ethernet rather than wifi. Browser OTA uploads are fussy about a weak link in either direction.

Tell me what the screen is doing and I will take the next step from there.
i got this message

I don't see anything attached on my end, just the text "i got this message".

Can you send it again, either as a screenshot or by typing the exact wording out? The precise text matters here, since an "invalid image" style message means something very different from a timeout or a network error.

And in the same reply, tell me whether the miner's screen is still showing its normal hashing display.
This is harlo_os_v2, not Harlo-OS firmware. Nothing was uploaded.

That message is good news actually, and it explains everything.

Your unit is safe: it refused the file and wrote nothing. What it is telling you is that the running 0.1.49 checks the image's project name, and this image identifies itself as harlo_os_v2, a different firmware line. An OTA can only replace firmware from its own line, so 0.1.49 will not take a 0.2.x image over the air.

That means the only way onto 0.2.101 is the browser factory flash, which is the exact step that is stalling for you on the BS-2 profile. So we are back to the one thing that is not on your side.

One last check worth doing, because it costs two minutes and rules out your network:

1. Open the flasher on a different computer, or on your phone, or on a different connection (phone hotspot).
2. Pick BS-2 and see whether it still hangs on "downloading and verifying".

If it hangs there too, it is the server, and JD already has it from me. If it suddenly works on another network, something local was blocking the download.

Keep your miner on 0.1.49 and hashing in the meantime. Nothing is at risk.
do i just use usbc cable from phone to miner?

No, do not flash from the phone. Phone browsers do not support Web Serial, which is what the flasher needs to talk to the board, so a USB-C cable from phone to miner will not work for flashing.

I meant the phone only as a way to test whether the download itself is blocked on your network. Clearer version:

1. Best test: same computer, but switch its internet to your phone's hotspot. Then open the flasher, pick BS-2, and see if it still hangs on "downloading and verifying".
2. Or try a second computer, if you have one, on any connection.

Either one uses Chrome or Edge on a computer, with a USB-C data cable from the computer to the miner.

If it still hangs on the hotspot, that settles it: the BS-2 image is not serving and it is JD's to fix.
i don't have another computer, and i think this is way over my head, i'll just keep using 0.1.49

That is a perfectly fine place to stop, and for the record none of this was over your head. You did everything right: you found the stall, pulled the OTA image, and the firmware itself told us why it refused. That is better diagnosis than most people get to.

0.1.49 is a working build and your miner keeps hashing on it, so you lose nothing by sitting there.

Where things stand: JD has the BS-2 image issue from me. When he fixes it, the flash is a two minute job, and if you want it done then, come back to this chat and I will walk you through it one step at a time. The team will also confirm by email.

Nothing for you to do until then. Just leave it running.
I appreciate your patience with me

Genuinely no patience needed, you were clear and you did every check I asked. That is what made it quick to narrow down.

Enjoy the BS-2, and come back here whenever you want to try the update again or if anything else comes up with it.
I thank you again, I really do I'm hoping the magic miner 40T is as awesome as it looks and reviews

It is a different class of machine from the BS-2, in a good way. 
It runs three modes up to about 50 TH/s, measured 41.4 TH/s at 690 W on a wall meter, around 50 dB in Eco mode, and it comes with Harlo OS built in.


Two practical things to plan for before it lands:

1. Power: at roughly 690 W flat out it wants its own outlet, not a shared strip with other miners. Eco mode pulls a lot less if you want it quieter and cooler.
2. Heat: it puts out real warmth, so give it a room that can take it rather than a closed cabinet.

And since it ships with Harlo OS already on it, setup is just wifi or Ethernet plus your pool details. If you want a hand configuring the pools when it arrives, come back here.
I have a question before you go though
Go ahead, I'm here. What's the question?
On Helium Deploy ads for Magic Miner 40T it says 30 chips but shows a picture of 36 chips and on description page for the 40T it says 28 chips.
Good catch, that is worth pinning down. Let me look at the product page myself.
Read the magic miner 40t page

Good catch, and worth being precise about. I just pulled the live product page.

What it says there, in two places: 
the spec list reads "ASIC: BM1370, 30 chips"
 and the modes table repeats 
BM1370, 30 chips
. So the ad and the current page agree at 30.

On the picture: the hero images on that page are product renders, not a board shot, so the number of squares you count on them is not a spec. I would not read a chip count off them.

The 28 is the one I cannot account for. Two things would help:

1. Where exactly did you see 28, which page or which section, so it can be found and corrected.
2. A screenshot if you still have it.

For what it is worth, the arithmetic favours 30: 40 TH/s across 30 BM1370 gives about 1.33 TH per chip, which is right where that chip sits. 28 would need about 1.43 TH each, which is high for stock settings.

I am sending this to JD so the number gets confirmed from the build and any page that disagrees gets fixed.
Handed to the team · Spec inconsistency across Magic Miner 40T listings; needs the authoritative chip

The team has it and will confirm by email, usually within one business day. If you stay in this chat, they can answer you here directly.

If you can point me at where the 28 appeared in the meantime, send it over and I will add it.
lol, page has been updated it now shows 30 chips, you guys are way ahead of me

Ha, that was quick. So 30 chips it is, and the pages now agree.

Thanks for flagging it, that is the kind of thing that only gets caught when someone actually reads the specs carefully.

So, two open items on your side: the BS-2 image fix with JD, and a 40T to look forward to. Come back here whenever either one needs a hand.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

I opened it. It is the Facebook/Instagram Reels ad: headline "Same BM1370. 30 Of Them.", a chip panel beside the 40T tower labelled "1 CHIP" on the single chip and "30 CHIPS" on the panel, and the line "The Bitaxe chip, times 30. Up to 50 TH/s. $16 per terahash", with (address hidden), Fri Sep 18, 12 PM ET, 50 units.

So the ad says 30 too, in both the headline and the label. The grid in the render is partly hidden behind the tower, which is probably where a different count came from when you eyeballed it, and that art is illustrative rather than a photo of the board.

Bottom line: 30 BM1370, consistent across the ad and the product page now. JD has it to confirm against the build anyway, so if anything differs you will hear it.
is that one chip in picture or is that showing all the chips

Both, side by side. That is the point the ad is making.

- Bottom left, the little chip on a small green board with the "1 CHIP" label: that is one BM1370, which is what a single Bitaxe has.
- The flat panel of squares next to the tower, labelled "30 CHIPS": that is all thirty of them shown together, to say the 40T has thirty of that same chip.

It is a comparison graphic, not a photo of the inside. The real 40T does not have a flat plate of chips like that, they sit on boards behind the heatsink in the tower. The panel is just an easy way to show thirty of one thing against one of the same thing.
ok, but there is 36 on the panel

You may well be right, and I am not going to argue with someone who actually counted. If that grid is 6 by 6, the render shows 36 squares while the label next to it says 30. That would be an error in the artwork, not in the machine.

The spec is the thing that counts: BM1370, 30 chips, on the product page and in the ad's own headline and label. And 40 TH/s across 30 of those chips is right for that silicon, where 36 would not be.

JD already has this from me, including the image showing 36, so the art can get fixed. Good eye, twice in one afternoon.
Thank you again for your time, i truly appreciate you guys

You are very welcome, and thank you for the sharp eyes today.

Leave the BS-2 hashing on 0.1.49, and when the image is sorted come straight back here and we will do the update together.

Enjoy the 40T when it lands.
I will, have a great day and an awesome weekend
You too, enjoy the weekend. Happy hashing.
